The day at a glance

Leaves the irrigated valley floor almost immediately. Most of the day is oak savanna and cattle ranching through Jolon and the Fort Hunter Liggett country — dry-farmed and thinly settled, which is why there is so little on the route. Vineyards reappear on the approach to Paso Robles.

Worth looking up for

  • Remote oak country through Jolon and the Nacimiento backcountry, with no highway miles at all.
  • Lake Nacimiento appears on the descent toward Paso Robles.

What to watch for

  • The hardest day: 62.6 mi, 4,005 ft, and only 4% shade. Start as early as you can.
  • No mapped water anywhere on the route, and effectively nothing between mile 1 and mile 48. This is the day the SAG car matters most.
  • Steepest sustained pitch of the trip at mi 42.2–43.8, 639 ft at 7.5% — and it comes late.
